# Service

`c.Service` calls the API's Service group. The services of the host: systemd on
Linux, launchd on macOS.

### List

```go
func (s *ServiceService) List(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
) (*Response[Collection[ServiceEntry]], error)
```

List the services of the host.

Lists each service that systemd has loaded, with its state, whether it starts at
boot and its description, through gohai. A service that osapi deployed shows by
the name it was deployed with, not its unit's osapi- name, and is managed. On a
Mac, it lists each daemon that launchd has loaded in the system domain, by its
label. A daemon that osapi deployed reads by the name it was deployed with, app
for io.osapi.app.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/service`, and needs the permission
`service:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A service that osapi deployed reads by its name, `go run service.go list`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.List(ctx, target)
```

### Create

```go
func (s *ServiceService) Create(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input ServiceCreateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[ServiceResult]], error)
```

Deploy a service.

Gets the object from the object store and writes it as the unit file of the
service, such as /etc/systemd/system/osapi-app.service for app, then reloads
systemd. A unit file at that path that osapi did not write, such as the agent's
own osapi-agent.service, is refused. A unit file that already has the content
does not change. The service does not start: start and enable are their own
actions. On a Mac, the object is the plist of the daemon,
/Library/LaunchDaemons/io.osapi.app.plist for app, with the label io.osapi.app,
and launchd does not load it until start.

It sends `POST /api/node/{hostname}/service`, and needs the permission
`service:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Deploy a unit file, `go run service.go create`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Create(ctx, target, client.ServiceCreateInput{
	Name:   "app",
	Object: "app.service",
})
```

Deploy a plist on a Mac, `go run service.go create-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Create(ctx, target, client.ServiceCreateInput{
	Name:   "app",
	Object: "app.plist",
})
```

### Get

```go
func (s *ServiceService) Get(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[ServiceEntry]], error)
```

Get one service.

Reads one service from the same list, by its name with .service or without it. A
service that osapi deployed reads by the name it was deployed with, such as app,
as its writes take it, or by its unit's name, osapi-app. A service that systemd
has not loaded is not found. On a Mac, a daemon that osapi deployed and launchd
has not loaded is dead.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/service/{name}`, and needs the permission
`service:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A running service, `go run service.go get`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Get(ctx, target, "ssh")
```

A name with .service, `go run service.go get-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Get(ctx, target, "ssh.service")
```

A service that osapi deployed, by the name it was deployed with,
`go run service.go get-3`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Get(ctx, target, "app")
```

A service that osapi deployed, by its unit's name, `go run service.go get-4`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Get(ctx, target, "osapi-app")
```

A daemon on a Mac, by its label, `go run service.go get-5`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Get(ctx, target, "com.apple.cron")
```

### Update

```go
func (s *ServiceService) Update(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input ServiceUpdateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[ServiceResult]], error)
```

Deploy a new unit file for a service.

Writes the object as the unit file of a service that osapi deployed, then
reloads systemd when the file changed. A service that osapi did not deploy is
not found. On a Mac, it writes the plist, and a daemon that runs keeps its old
plist until restart.

It sends `PUT /api/node/{hostname}/service/{name}`, and needs the permission
`service:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

A new unit file, `go run service.go update`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Update(ctx, target, client.ServiceUpdateInput{
	Name:   "app",
	Object: "app-v2.service",
})
```

A new plist on a Mac, `go run service.go update-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Update(ctx, target, client.ServiceUpdateInput{
	Name:   "app",
	Object: "app-v2.plist",
})
```

### Delete

```go
func (s *ServiceService) Delete(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[ServiceResult]], error)
```

Remove a service that osapi deployed.

Stops and disables the service, removes its unit file and reloads systemd. A
service with no unit file does not change. On a Mac, it boots the daemon out of
launchd when it is loaded, and removes its plist.

It sends `DELETE /api/node/{hostname}/service/{name}`, and needs the permission
`service:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Remove a service, `go run service.go delete`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Delete(ctx, target, "app")
```

A unit file that osapi did not deploy, `go run service.go delete-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Delete(ctx, target, "agent")
```


### Enable

```go
func (s *ServiceService) Enable(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	name string,
) (*Response[Collection[ServiceResult]], error)
```

Make a service that osapi deployed start at boot.

Enables the service. A service that is enabled does not change, and nor does a
unit with no [Install] section, which systemd calls static: it cannot start at
boot. A service that osapi did not deploy is not found.

It sends `POST /api/node/{hostname}/service/{name}/enable`, and needs the
permission `service:execute`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Enable the service, `go run service.go enable`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Enable(ctx, target, "app")
```

A unit with no [Install] section, `go run service.go enable-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.Service.Enable(ctx, target, "static")
```

permission `service:execute`.

## Types

The fields of each type are the properties of its schema in the API's spec.

### RowStatus

What happened on the host: ok, the operation ran and succeeded; failed, it ran
and did not succeed; skipped, the host's OS family does not support it; timeout,
the host did not answer, so nobody knows whether it ran.

A `string`, one of `ok`, `failed`, `skipped`, `timeout`.
